verdict.rationale: Fly.io converts Docker images into fast-booting, hardware-isolated VMs that run globally close to users, and Sprites give each workload a full Linux box. A full VM is not a restricted runtime subset, so arbitrary code can run at the edge. However, the evidence never names Node.js or npm, and the model is VMs/containers rather than a documented serverless-functions product. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of unmodified Node.js/npm support, a serverless function-style deployment model, and independent hands-on corroboration of running full Node workloads at the edge.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run unmodified Node.js code and npm packages in edge/serverless functions instead of a restricted runtime subset

citations.quote: Fly.io converts Docker images to fast-booting VMs and runs them globally.
Fly Machines are hardware-isolated VMs that boot in under a second, run close to your users, and scale out to tens of thousands when the traffic arrives.
Every agent gets its own Linux box.
Run it in a hardware-isolated VM. A clean baseline per request, so no two users ever share state.
